name: CA-18
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by sixteen points
Lofgren holds a roughly 28-to-1 fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 99%
No public polling; rating rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: A sixteen-point Democratic district, a long-serving well-funded incumbent, and a challenger who has raised about $60,000 with minimal cash on hand leave no visible path to an upset; markets price the Democratic win near certain.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or a sudden influx of challenger money would be the main signal to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Zoe Lofgren, a long-serving Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a San Jose-area district that leans Democratic by sixteen points. She enters the general election with about $643,000 on hand after raising roughly $1.7 million, supplemented by outside support, while Republican Shane Lewis has raised about $60,000 and reports only a few thousand dollars in cash. No public polls or expert ratings are available for the race, and prediction markets put the chance of a Democratic win near ninety-nine percent.

The combination of a strongly favorable district, incumbency, and an overwhelming financial edge leaves the challenger with little visible path. The forecast rates the seat Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any specific sign of competitiveness.
